notes.text: The authorial page number is 24; a pale bottom-left foliation reads 56 and is represented separately. The page begins in mid-sentence. The manuscript gives an ensemble with N(x)+1 elements and writes N(x)=card(Sigma_{< or <= x}); the comparison sign remains open. It then displays an application-but and a tuple sent to its final entry. The author identifies the fibre of x with the displayed P_d expression. The P font and the cardinality subscript are not silently settled, and the displayed counting assertion has not been independently verified.

The manuscript says that the relative structure of Sigma(1) over Sigma=Sigma(0) is that of an ens tot. ordonné relatif, allowing the system of Sigma(d) and its cofinal semi-simplicial applications to be reconstituted. The slanted margin says: Tout ceci est donc à faire indépendt de toute condition topologique. The local superscripts are retained occurrence by occurrence, with clear stars at système des and Les espaces and explicit uncertainty at several compact forms. The isolated sign below the bare Sigma is recorded without assigning it a mathematical role.

In the paragraph marked by a circled c, the author writes that the inserted B_alpha, described by the inserted word bordants, correspond through a circled reference to points z_alpha over x and are mutually transverse, et à fortiori distincts. The next paragraph says that intersections of certain B_alpha correspond to points of Sigma(d) over x as images of the indicated germs. Both b labels have separate underlines. The first horizontal mark remains open as line or arrow, and the second has a visibly unheaded shaft. These are reports of the manuscript’s claims and marks, without an independent transversality or correspondence proof.

The closing passage speaks of Les espaces Sigma*(d), the applications 1/2 simpliciales cofinales, and the relative space with its order structure, ending est décrit entièrement at the page edge. A small cancelled glyph before Les, the cancelled dit proposal, and the final cancelled satisfa fragment are preserved. The last fragment has a residual loop after f; it has not been completed into a word. No mathematical theorem was checked in making these readings.
